segment.source: Xit! We're under attack!<end>
Xer.<end>
::He stares through you, holding a t-flask filled with mushroom brew.:: Xit. All of it.<end>
Eh, you new, $(#man/sis)?<end>
Sorry, I've got a lotta work right now.<end>
<end>
No hard feelings, $(#man/sis).<end>
Good luck. Xile.<end>
Thanks for everything you did for the expedition, $(#man/sis). <end>
Done. <end>
I managed to recover some interesting stuff. <end>
<end>
<end>
Hey, I'm sorry about being a jerk earlier.<end>
Sorry?<end>
*Really* sorry.<end>
Well, 'kay. We've been through a lot of crap together. No <end>
point in holding grudges. We're a team, right, $(#man/sis)?<end>
<end>
Want some coffee now?<end>
I sure would.<end>
'Kay, 'kay. I'm kind of busy with stuff here, so feel free to go to my tent and grab yourself a flask or two from the coffeemaker. <end>
And leave something for me.<end>
Thanks, Seeger.<end>
No problem. <end>
Enjoy your coffee, $(#man/sis). Xcell.<end>
How long do the t-flasks retain heat?<end>
Huh... ::He nods a few times.:: A long time. <end>
'Kay then, $(#man/sis), 'kay. Grab yourself a flask or two from the coffeemaker. And leave something for me.<end>
I would very much like some coffee.<end>
'Kay, 'kay. The coffeemaker's in my tent. I'm kind of busy with stuff here, so feel free to go there and grab yourself a flask or two. <end>

'Kay. ::He goes to his coffeemaker and presses a button: As the coffee is poured into the t-flask, the air slowly becomes wonderfully saturated with its smell; after a few moments you have in your hands a t-flask full of smoking hot coffee.::<end>
::Gaze at it in awe.::<end>
::He observes you with satisfying interest.:: Well... <end>
Can I get some more coffee?<end>
If you weren't such an xer earlier, I'd give it to you. But since you walked out on me...<end>
<end>
How was I an *xer*, whatever that means? You're the offensive one!<end>
You overreacted, that's how. You were an *xer*. Simple.<end>
Emotions. I'm sorry.<end>
You know what, I don't need your dumb fancy coffee anyway.<end>
Fine by me, $(#man/sis). Fine by me. ::He turns away from you.::<end>
Well...<end>
I opened the Keep and gave you more reasons to drink it.<end>
Huh? Oh! Ha-ha, yeah. ::He scratches the back of his head.::<end>
I think I earned it by now.<end>
Yeah, that you certainly did. Xcell. <end>
More, huh? Nnnn-I don't think so, $(#man/sis).<end>
I'm not exactly swimming in this stuff. Coffee beans don't grow on rocks, you know. Xem.<end>
Perhaps later. But don't forget your offer.<end>
I won't. Don't worry.<end>
::[Persuade]:: *Really* sorry.<end>
Better. Kay', no <end>
::He takes a sip of coffee.:: Not bying it.<end>
Professor Oldfield wants to know if you've compiled the recovered data for him.<end>

We were under attack, $(#man/sis). Now, I may be a kind of person that rarely lifts my ass from the chair, but even I'm not that xtreme to sit here and sift through this stuff while people are dying... like, around me.<end>

::He turns to the computer and opens a file, sighing.::
But yeah, I do have some of the important bits sorted. I'll send it to him as soon as the network's ba-- ::He glances at one of his monitors and raises his eyebrows.:: Oh, Marcus sorted the power. Xtra, xtra... Sending it now.<end>
What is this about, really? The data. The professor mentioned it's some kind of a breakthrough discovery.<end>

Oh, yes, you betcha. You see, ever since we got here we've been trying to find a way to enter that building just across from my tent - the Keep. The panel by the gate is totally unresponsive, and the walls are xtremely thick and sturdy - hey, the building did survive the Biocorp assault on the island after all; and, you know, we don't just want to blow things up here unless we really, really - really gotta.<end>

Now, the building's still got power, 'kay, as we're easily picking that up on our instruments, but so far we haven't found a way to interface with that panel. Until I recovered this data. According to it, the panel is actually a scanner which authenticates a person based on a small active radio-frequency identification, or A-RFID, microchip that is most often implanted in the right hand. So, if we find one of these microchips or learn to--
Wait an xin' second... Why am I telling you all this?<end>
Do go on.<end>

Well... 'kay.
We find a working chip and we're in. All other NFT facilities should work the same way, so we'll be able to gain access to those as well... if we can get through the natives. <end>
Anyway, it seems every NFT citizen had an implant. These implants also contained some other, personal data, but that is of secondary importance right now.<end>
So where do we find one of these chips?<end>

Now *that's* the-- ::An ascending two-note sound interrupts your conversation, and something flashes on the bottom of his right screen.::
Xcuse me for a moment. It's the professor.<end>

::He puts his coffee aside and his headset on, adjusts the microphone and clicks the icon flashing on his screen. A window pops up, its top right corner bearing what appears to be the University of Dis logo - an outline of a frontal view of a grandiose building placed in a circle, under which "University of Dis" is written in a serif font. Then the face of Professor Oldfield appears, speaking words only Seeger can hear.::
Yes, sir?
You did?<end>

::He turns to you, still talking to the Professor.::
Huh? Yes, $(#he/she)'s here...
I'll tell $(#him/her).<end>

::He is still facing you, but his gleaming eyes are looking through you.::
Oh, thank you, sir.
::He smiles.:: I know.
I am well aware of that, sir. Xcell.
I... dropped the comm once the attack started and broke it.
Yes, yes, I understand.<end>
What did the Professor say?<end>

::Just as you open your mouth, his face disappears behind a broad smile.::
Really?
Yes, sir. Thank you again, sir. Xtra! Yes, yes, I'll tell $(#him/her) what you said. Goodbye.<end>
What did the Professor say?<end>
That you should see him now.<end>
Anyway, you stopped at: "Now *that's* the--".<end>
Actually, the professor will fill you in on the rest.<end>
Come on, man, this is getting ridiculous!<end>
Y-- You better go see the professor.<end>
Damn it. See ya.<end>
'Kay. See ya.<end>
I better get going then.<end>
Felt like he said a lot more than that.<end>
Yes, but not to you.<end>
Because I asked you.<end>
::Gesture him to proceed.::<end>
I have to know everything if I'm going to do this job right.<end>
What do you do around here?<end>

Well, I'm the person who gets called when a cooler in someone's desktop is "louder than ass," when a mobile "ain't working right" due to fat finger syndrome - and inappropriate usage in general - or when "I lost all mah data 'cause the power died," when in fact his data is fine, he just doesn't know where he's been saving it. ::He sighs.::<end>
What I was actually brought here to do is data recovery, decryption, analysis. Xcell. But some people don't realize that and bug me about each and every triviality they encounter. <end>
Thankfully, all of that is about to come to an end. Xile.<end>
So if your mobile is acting funky - please leave me out of it. Xile.<end>
Is that coffee you're drinking?<end>
This? Yes. Why? <end>
Never seen coffee before?<end>
I have. <end>

::He pauses, watching you while a pillar of smoke from the hot coffee pirouettes between you and him. With commiseration in his eyes, he softly proceeds.::
You... don't have any coffee beans here?<end>
Coffee *beans*?<end>

Wow. I'm sorry. I knew things were bad here, but this bad? Xit. *X*. *it*. But you have, like, hydroponics, right? You are capable of growing certain plants here? Then why no real coffee? I don't get it.<end>
My home station has hydroponics, but I haven't seen many elsewhere.<end>

::He shakes his head in.:: $(#No man/No one) should live without good xin' coffee.
You know, I got some more here. ::He glances at the coffeemaker on the other table.:: <end>
If you weren't such an xer earlier, I'd offer you some. But since you walked out on me...<end>
You want one?<end>
::Shrug.::<end>
They're not so bad after you get used to them, but what you've got here... is something else.<end>
We pour some horrible synthetic powder into hot water and drink it like that.<end>
No.<end>
I suppose there are somewhere, but I haven't seen it during my humble life.<end>
That coffee you're drinking...<end>
This? <end>
About that coffee...<end>
Hey, could you take a look at this for me?<end>
<end>
<end>

::He carefully grasps the slimy tablet with two fingers.::
Hm, yes... <end>
I can extract data from these kinds of devices - MPCs. This looks like a work tablet, but there are smaller, foldable devices as well. Neat little things. If you come across more of these<end>
, bring them to me.<end>
Can they be repaired?<end>

Hardly. These things are *old*. But their data storage drives - now *those* things are high quality. While a lot of data does end up being unrecoverable in the end, I've had great success so far. You just bring me MPCs and I'll put everything I manage to recover <end>
on that PC over there. ::He points to the computer next to his own.:: That one. <end>
Feel free to browse the files once I'm done.<end>
In fact, you know, there is one already there. It's from one of NFT soldier's MPCs. Check it out.<end>
'Kay now... let's see what we got.<end>
::Wait.::<end>
on my PC in the tent. <end>
'Kay. I'll get to work straight away.<end>
Ah, those are MPCs. Give them here. <end>
I can extract data from these neat little devices, so if you come across more of them<end>
Ah, that's an MPC. Give it here. <end>
You're using some strange words I'm not familiar with. The ones starting with "x."<end>
After what you did... Nah, $(#man/sis). <end>
I'll cooperate, but it's best we skip the chit-chat.<end>

Oh, like xtreme and xit? It's... complicated. It's Hexagonian X-- *Slang*. Sorry, I totally forgot you're a Southerner and you don't know about that stuff. I mean, don't take it the wrong way, $(#man/sis), it's just that you people prefer the Arena, 'kay, since that's what you have here. I mean, not because one is worse than the... uh, than the other. Actually, it's not a really good comparison at all because of the... um... you know.<end>
I should just... I mean, stop talking now. Forget I said anything. ::Silence.::<end>
It's alright. No need to stress over it, man.<end>
I am not stressed at all. ::He takes a sip from his t-flask and shakes his head sideways, vacantly staring forward.:: Not at all.<end>
I find what you said deeply offensive.<end>
Oh, come on. Are you serious?<end>
Of course not. Only morons get offended by stuff like that. Relax.<end>
Xit! I actually believed you for a moment. ::He takes a sip.:: You aren't so bad after all.<end>
::Stare at him silently.::<end>
'Kay. My girlfriend does that often. Stares. Angrily. Hey, it's what they do.<end>
Look, I'm sorry for offending you. It wasn't my intention. My tongue sometimes gets a head start on my brain. That's all I can say. Sorry, $(#man/sis).<end>
It's alright. We're good. There were more things I wanted to talk to you about.<end>
::He nods with a smile.:: Xcell. <end>
Go for it.<end>
I gotta go now. See you later.<end>
So that's how we're gonna play. <end>
And I even made coffee for you. <end>
Xer.<end>
::Leave without saying anything.::<end>
How about we simply change the subject?<end>
'Kay, 'kay!<end>
Tell me about Hexagon.<end>
You know, $(#man/sis), maybe some other time. It's kind of a broad topic and I've got work to do.<end>
Some other time. ::He sips some coffee.::<end>

While Dis may be the capital of North Underrail, Hexagon is the capital of technology. It's like this microcosm of everything high-tech, a place where you could find pretty much every-xtreme-thing, 'kay.<end>
So how did you end up in there?<end>

A friend of mine took me there. We needed some network equipment, and one of his acquaintances there had the best stuff.
Hexagon's a pretty confusing place. It's like this tall tower with many floors, each one packed with narrow, maze-like passages leading to all sorts of these... xtra places.<end>

Naturally the place is home to all kinds of tech gangs and various factions; the Protectorate got no presence there, nope. You gotta be careful where you tread and who you're dealing with, 'cause if you're not, you might find yourself face to face with... I don't know, a cyborg mugger - or a tech harvester. ::He makes a grimace.::
Usually I'd stay out of that place, but that friend... he knows his way around. I just kept my head down and followed.<end>
But then, after I was introduced to XR, I bought this living cube in-- ::And then he shuts up.::<end>
Go on.<end>
Forget I mentioned it. It's just some meaningless Hexagonian slang.<end>
Forget about it, $(#man/sis).<end>
::He looks around.:: 'Kay. But don't tell anyone about this. People don't... understand this kind of stuff.<end>
And you, Toddo, this is not for your ears!<end>
::He confirms his understanding with a few quick nods.::<end>
'Kay. XR is short for mixed reality. That's *miXed Reality*.<end>
::[Intelligence]:: You mean, something between virtual and actual reality?<end>
::He nods.:: Something like that, yeah. But this is different. <end>
This is *xcell*!<end>
You know how regular virtual reality works already: <end>
You put on a headset, maybe connect the electrodes, enter a gyrosphere if you got it, and then you're in this totally computer-generated world.<end>

But miXed Reality is different: Some of it is real, some of it is virtual. ::He glances around once again before proceeding.:: 'Kay, now, there's this thing called a *miXR* you gotta step into. It's like a gyrosphere, but there are no headsets, electrodes or anything you have to put on.
You step into it, the entrance closes - and the session starts. <end>
It costs a lot of credits, but it's worth it, $(#man/sis). Hexagonians are going crazy over it.<end>
Down here we'd say "going derailed."<end>
Sure. Xrailed, hah.<end>
I still don't understand the *mixed* part. What are these sessions like?<end>

Yeah, so, when you're in virtual reality, everything's digital; the computer reacts to what you do - you affect the virtual. But in mixed reality - the real things can... get affected by virtual things.<end>
How is that even possible?<end>

I don't know. No one knows - that's why it's so xcell! Everything around you changes, and you can't even tell you're inside the miXR anymore. You can feel the air currents, smell things, touch, taste, feel.
The sessions themselves range from just visiting places, meeting people, flying, doing... all kinds of things.<end>
<end>
Flying? As in piloting an aircraft?<end>
Nah... *Flying*.<end>
You can get abilities you never knew were possible! You can see things beyond real, virtual - you can't even tell.<end>

::His voice drops almost to a whisper.:: There are... also some dark things going on in XR. People... some people get killed in the miXRs. Things that are brought in end up somewhere else. Some people disappear.
I stay away from those kind of sessions. I don't have the courage for that. Where I go to, I do some Dreadnought piloting... and some other things.<end>
Other things? Like "*you know what*"?<end>
That? No, no, no, no, no! Some do, but I... haven't found a good-- Not that I was looking for it. I'd try it, but-- I haven't.<end>
Anyway, this whole mystery, the possibilites, everything I told you about miXed Reality is why it's so thrilling. That's why the Hexagonians are going <end>
derailed over it. <end>
Part of it is real, part of it isn't.<end>
Who made XR and the miXRs? That has got to be some *advanced* technology.<end>

::He shrugs.:: No one's got a clue. It just suddenly appeared, and now it's here and everyone who knows about it is spending all their credits on it.
I'm new to all of this, $(#man/sis), so I know little, but I think one of the factions there is pushing this. Just a rumor, 'kay.<end>
Could all of this simply be a combination of a good illusion and some false rumors spread around as to hype the whole XR thing up?<end>
I... haven't thought about it. Everything's so real, but... Hmmm...<end>

::He pauses, sipping his coffee.:: Xit.
No, no, no, it can't be. I know what I experienced. But then again... But it can't... ::He sips some more coffee.::<end>
::Say nothing.::<end>
So there. Now you know. And remember, keep this to yourself, 'kay?<end>
crazy over it. <end>
That sounds interesting, actually.<end>
Seems boring.<end>
Listen: <end>
::[Hacking]:: Is it something like augmented reality? Real environments with a computer-generated overlays?<end>
You're thinking in the right direction, but this is something different. <end>
What's that?<end>
You know what virtual reality is, don't you? <end>
XR?<end>
Is this the virtual reality Professor Oldfield mentioned?<end>
Tell me about Hexagon. Professor already told me a bit but I'd like to hear more.<end>
He did? 'Kay. ::He shrugs.:: <end>
I'd like to know what XR is.<end>
What can you tell me about A-RFID microchips?<end>

A-RFID stands for active radio frequency identification. Basically, it means that the microchip has its own power source, as opposed to passive chips, which get powered by a reader. The data I've recovered - with a lot of effort - tells me that NFT used these chips originally for storing personal and medical history, to monitor the host's health status and to keep track of their location. I don't know how the microchip is being powered, by a battery or even by the host himself, but I bet they did a good job on it considering everyone's got them.<end>
So, when did authorization come into the picture?<end>

The log mentions just that. It seems that the NFT didn't really have much need for authorization checks, 'kay, but they implemented this system to make it more difficult for Biocorp to enter their facilities. Considering they never made it into the Keep, it worked.<end>
::[Intelligence]:: You said a microchip tracks the host's health status. What if they made it so a microchip won't work without a live host?<end>

Huh...That makes sense. So you can't just chop someone's hand off and use it to pass authorization. And besides, if the microchips *are* being powered by the host's body, they might not even work at all. They could be powered by other means then, but what if they self-destruct if they've been left unpowered for a while, as a precaution. Xit!<end>
Well, we'll figure it all out once we find one of the microchips. If nothing else, maybe it'll help us learn how to trick the system. In any case, we need it, 'kay.<end>
It seems that the implant does not need a live host to function. It's neither being powered by the host nor is a living one necessary to pass the authentication and authorization checks.<end>

Luckily for us, that appears to be the case. That's xcell right there! It probably has a battery. As for the second, either it's an oversight on NFT's part or... I don't know, there could be something we're missing.
Have you tried pulling the hand out of the glove, huh?<end>
No. I'd rather not touch it if I don't need to.<end>
I hear you. It's... xtreme. Damn. Xit.<end>
Anyway, I'll, you know, take one of the microchips from a body in the Keep and figure out how the thing is working, 'kay. Once I've got time. I'll let you know what I've discovered.<end>
I extracted the microchip from the severed hand...<end>

::He loses some color just by thinking about it.::
Xtreme... But what for?<end>
I needed to implant it into myself. It turns out I was wrong - the host does indeed power the implant.<end>

Huh? Hold on, but how did you manage to open the Keep and all of those other facilities with a microchip implanted into a severed arm? I don't know how it is down here, but in North Underrail severed arms tend to be... lifeless, 'kay.<end>
Well, it turns out there was something living inside that glove... ::Explain to him the microchip extraction process, with all the nasty details.::<end>

::And so, each sentence that comes out of your mouth further bleaches Seeger's face until unhealthy shades of green begin to appear.::
Xit...
::...is the only word he uses for the duration of your talk.::<end>

::After you're done with the story, he takes a moment to wipe his forehead before saying something other than "xit".::
'Kay...<end>
So... the sterilization chemical killed it? ::He twiches his hand as a reference to your story.:: Like it were some kind of a virus?<end>
It could be that, it could be everything: exposure to air, the needle and, yes, the chemical.<end>

Xit.
::He takes a sip of coffee, appearing as though he is sipping some color back into his face.::
You know what? Let's not talk about this ever again.<end>
Xile...<end>
I needed to implant it into myself. Turns out the host does indeed power the implant.<end>
I'll leave you to your work.<end>
Appreciate it. Bye.<end>
Sending it to Professor Oldfield straight away. <end>
Got something interesting for you. <end>
It's on the PC.<end>
You can check it out on the PC in my tent.<end>

::An alluring scent invites you inside: It's rich, pleasant and strong enough to draw a hopper out of its crevice; it's like coffee - but smells infinitely better than the dark-brown dust-mixed-with-water consumed throughout South Underrail. This - this is something from the North.
And if the delightful aroma is any indication, tasting it has got to be quite an experience.::<end>

::You take a step toward the man sitting at the desk, looking at letters and numbers and symbols of various kinds scrolling across his screen. He hears you and turns around, and in his hand - a t-flask of smoking black liquid. It *is* coffee after all.::
Yo, you need something?<end>
Are you Jeremy Seeger? Professor Oldfield told me to see you.<end>
Yeah. The one. <end>
You... gotta be one of the new sec-troopers, huh? Welcome to the Hell's Gut, $(#man/sis). That name seems more and more appropriate the more time we spend here. Am I right now?<end>
Well... anyway, what've you got for me?<end>
Who are you?<end>
Seeger. Jeremy Seeger. <end>
Nope, wrong tent. Goodbye.<end>
'Kay. ::He returns to his work.::<end>
Yes?<end>
<end>
::With a trembling voice.:: You... go see Chief Briggs down there.<end>

::He takes a sip of coffee, holding the cup with both of his trembling hands.::
Xit! It's all my fault.
I could've been taken away down there - or xed on the spot! ::He looks at his t-flask with gratitude.:: But I went to get some coffee. Saved my *X*.<end>
<end>
I needed to ask you something.<end>
Sorry, $(#man/sis), I'm xin' out so hard right now. I can't even think straight.<end>
Calm down. I'll see you later.<end>
::He nods.::<end>
I'll get the professor back, don't you worry.<end>
::Nod and leave.::<end>
I have something I want you to take a look at.<end>
What's going on? Any news on the professor?<end>
<end>
::You find Seeger packing his equipment, scratching his head in wonder as to why a particular device won't fit the box.:: <end>
::He occasionally glances at Todd, who is amusing himself with a mobile computer bearing a Unversity of Dis logo, himself also furtively glancing at the coffeemaker.::<end>
Hey! Coffee is no, no! Professor *kill* Jeremy - *keeeel* - if Todd drink coffee and gets sick, blaaaurgh.<end>
Uh... why are you talking funny?<end>
Just don't touch the xin' coffee, 'kay.<end>

::He then turns to you.::
Hey, $(context.player.Name).<end>
<end>
Having some fun with Todd, I see.<end>
He's xcell. I'm just... "On the X," as they say. Don't want him hurting himself.<end>
I just came to say goodbye.<end>
Oh yeah?<end>
There was something I needed from you before we get out of here.<end>
Go ahead. Just keep it quick, <end>

I gotta pack this stuff up and, of course, I gotta do it all by myself.
And I'm not keen on being left behind. Xile.<end>

Hey, you were xcell, $(#man/sis). If it wasn't for you I'd still be pulling creepy-crawlies out of my hair.
<end>
If you need something, now's your last chance. <end>
::The computers and the coffeemaker are the last to go, it seems.::<end>
::He's still packing his equipment. ::<end>
<end>
Oh. You're back. <end>
::His t-flask is beside him, but the coffee is cold.::<end>
::He takes a sip of coffee.::<end>
Hey, $(#man/sis). Make it quick. <end>
Huh? <end>
::He lifts his head a bit, then turns around completely.:: Oh, it's you. What've you got for me? <end>
Got something for me, $(context.player.Name)? <end>
<end>
<end>

::You find him perusing through several medium-sized plastic boxes filled with assorted electronic gadgetry while intermittently and nervously scratching his neck.::
Xit! Can't believe we're out.<end>
What's the matter?<end>
Oh, hey there. Nothing... ::He looks at one of the boxes again.:: It's just that we're running out of electronics. I hate it when I don't have stuff.<end>
::He then turns to you.:: What've you got for me?<end>
Hey, Seeger. I came to talk to you about something.<end>
Oh, hey there. What've you got for me?<end>
Hey, could you take a look at this for me?<end>
Oh, it's you. Let me see...<end>
::Leave.::<end>
::He stares unwantingly at his t-flask of coffee.:: Xit.<end>
Something wrong?<end>
::He looks at you.:: We're being xterminated.<end>

::He rubs his left eye and yawns.::
<end>

I'm not going down there again. Xit. I somehow got over the dead bodies, but angry pirates...? ::He takes a nervous sip.::
Xem!<end>

What's next, the natives? No thanks. I'll stay here.
<end>
Now, what've you got for me?<end>
<end>
Let me tell you... ::He takes a sip of coffee.:: This tent might not be much, but I'll take it over those creepy offices down there any day of the week.<end>

::He flinches and spills some of his coffee over his pants.::
XIT, XIT, XIT!<end>
::Wait.::<end>

::He pulls down his trainers to his knees, revealing deep-black underpants with overlapping columns of bright green symbols. He grabs a filthy handkerchief from his pocket and starts rubbing the stains.::
You scared the crap outta me!<end>
I'd say I scared the trainers off ya.<end>
Funny, huh? ::He makes a grimace.:: I almost burned my... bits. <end>
::He pulls up his trainers.:: What is it, $(#man/sis)?<end>
Are you okay?<end>
Yes, yes. <end>
This time you got something for me...<end>
Uh... ::He awkwardly conceals his underpants.:: 'Kay.<end>
I need something from you, Seeger.<end>
Stop fooling around, Seeger.<end>
Xit, $(#man/sis) - I'm burning! <end>
Hey, Seeger. I came to talk to you about something.<end>
Hey, could you take a look at this for me?<end>

::He stares at the screen, twisting one of his locks of hair with his index finger and mumbling to himself. He seems to be unaware of your presence.::
Data, data, data... so much data... and only one XeeGer, mhm, mhm.<end>

::He flinches.::
Xit! Uh, h-hey. Khm, uh, got something for me, $(#man/sis)?<end>
Xtreme, $(#man/sis)! We gotta get more of those Protectors on our side.<end>

::He walks outside and looks south toward the beach.:: Look at that bot saunter. Xtreme! ::He takes a sip and returns inside.::
What've you got for me?<end>
